answer: A cluster of fake identities spreading across the reef of accounts gains nothing, since splitting stake across many wallets only multiplies unbonding costs and slashing exposure. Sybil resistance here uses stake-weighted identity anchored to a bonded knoll of collateral: each agent must lock tokens before claiming rewards. Duplicate registrations are detected and their stake burned, rendering the attack a hollow investment. Attacker cost grows linearly with identity count, while honest single-stake agents pay once. In practice, Agent0252 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
